title: Thirteen years
hook: exile, disguise, the year in hiding

segments.voice: Yesterday: Draupadi's sari, the cloth that wouldn't end, and a question nobody in the hall could answer. Unending.

You'd think, after all that, the Pandavas would never touch dice again. Freed by Draupadi's wishes, they head home, and they're called back. One more game, one throw. The loser goes into the forest for twelve years, then spends a thirteenth year in hiding, somewhere in the world, undiscovered. If anyone recognizes them that year, they start all over again. Yudhishthira plays. Yudhishthira loses. And five royal brothers and a queen walk into the forest with nothing.
screen: `CALLED BACK FOR ONE MORE THROW.` → `TWELVE YEARS IN THE FOREST.` → `ONE MORE YEAR, UNSEEN.`

segments.voice: The twelve forest years fill a huge part of the Mahabharata: sages, pilgrimages, stories inside stories. Near the end of them, the brothers, desperately thirsty, find a lake guarded by a spirit, a yaksha, who says: answer my questions before you drink. Four brothers drink anyway and fall dead. Yudhishthira stops and answers. The most famous question: what is the greatest wonder in the world? His answer, roughly: every day people die all around us, and the rest of us live as if we never will. He answers well enough that his brothers are given back their lives. Then the thirteenth year. They go to the court of a king called Virata and hide in plain sight, each disguised as the last thing you'd expect. Yudhishthira, who lost everything at dice, becomes the king's dice companion. Bhima, the strongest man alive, becomes a cook. Arjuna, the great archer, lives as a dance teacher named Brihannala, in women's clothes, because of an old curse that now turns out to be a gift. The twins look after horses and cattle. And Draupadi, the queen, becomes a maid to the queen. It isn't safe. A powerful general of the court harasses Draupadi, and Bhima kills him in secret. But the year runs out, and they're not caught. Look at the disguises: each of them hides inside a smaller version of their own life. Sometimes the only way through is to disappear for a while, smaller, quieter, someone else, and wait. The year of hiding isn't the end of who they are. It's a year of carrying who they are, secretly.
screen: `THE YAKSHA'S QUESTIONS AT THE LAKE.` · `THE GREATEST WONDER.` · `HIDING IN PLAIN SIGHT.` · `A YEAR OF CARRYING WHO THEY ARE.`

segments.voice: Think of a season when you had to hide: what you believed, who you loved, how bad things were, or a job far beneath what you could do, kept quiet to stay safe. Remember what you carried in secret the whole time, and don't judge that season; it got you through. Then wonder who around you might be hiding right now, carrying something nobody sees.
Thirteen years. Twelve in the forest, and one in hiding, in plain sight, at a king's court.
Your line: the year of hiding. You don't always know what someone is carrying. Day seventy-four, done.

howItsDone: The Yaksha's questions to Yudhishthira are often retold and taught as a dialogue on dharma, and the Virata Parva, the book of the year in hiding, is traditionally recited in some regions to pray for rain.

chat.says: Why did the Pandavas hide as a cook and a dance teacher instead of fighting back?
options: The bet said a year in hiding, unrecognized, so each hid inside a smaller version of their life.
They had lost their strength in the forest years and could no longer fight at all.
They wanted to spy on King Virata and quietly take his kingdom for themselves.
chat.meaning: The terms were twelve years in the forest and a thirteenth hidden, undiscovered. Each disguise was a smaller version of who they were, carried in secret.

Yudhishthira.meaning: eldest Pandava brother, who lost everything at dice

yaksha.meaning: a nature spirit; here, the guardian of the lake

Virata.meaning: the king whose court hid the Pandavas for the thirteenth year

Bhima.meaning: the strongest Pandava brother, disguised as a cook

Brihannala.meaning: Arjuna's disguise as a dance teacher in women's clothes
